citations.claim: incoming speed just before ceiling bounce is ~32.97 upward
after bounce speed is ~40.34 downward, larger than incoming despite e=0.9 which should reduce it
total energy at first violating step exceeds allowed bound

counterfactual.change: changed body 0 restitution e from 0.9 to 0.0; without bounce amplification the failure disappears

explanation: Single body fired upward hits the ceiling boundary. Incoming speed ~32.97 at step 231 becomes outgoing ~40.34 at step 232, i.e. the boundary impulse amplifies velocity instead of scaling by e=0.9 (expected ~29.7). With no gravity loss over one substep and no controller work, this injects ~270 J, pushing total energy 924.2 over allowed 724.6 and violating energy_bound. Setting e=0 removes the amplification and the run passes.
vision_note: A single blue circle rises to the top edge and stays in contact with the ceiling across steps 229-231. At step 232 it appears just below the ceiling after rebounding, consistent with a ceiling bounce at the violation step.
